title: How much of what Terminal Delight needs from an emulator core does each candidate provide?

decision.statement: For each candidate terminal core, judge from the researched and checked evidence whether it provides each of thirteen things Terminal Delight's code needs from its emulator, so the decision matrix can show fit and migration cost per candidate with unknowns drawn as unknown.
decision.consumer: Parker, reading the fit columns of the terminal-core decision matrix
decision.acts_on_result: fills cells of the matrix; never ranks the cores (code does that with Parker's weights) and never chooses one
code_owns: Kitty feature coverage from the tags
not_decided_here: whether the evidence is true (claim-check owns that)

axes.means: An embedder can read each visible cell's character, its foreground and background colour, and its attribute flags (bold, italic, underline, inverse).
axes.consumer_uses_it_for: a must requirement in the fit column of the decision matrix

axes.means: An embedder can read the zero-width characters (combining marks) attached to a cell, or its whole grapheme cluster, not only its first character.
axes.consumer_uses_it_for: a must requirement in the fit column of the decision matrix

axes.means: An embedder can read a cell's underline colour, set by SGR 58, separately from its text colour.
axes.consumer_uses_it_for: a important requirement in the fit column of the decision matrix

axes.means: An embedder can tell which cells hold a double-width character and which are its second half.
axes.consumer_uses_it_for: a must requirement in the fit column of the decision matrix

axes.means: An embedder can read lines that have scrolled off the top into history (scrollback), not only the visible screen, whether through negative line indices, a history accessor or a scroll offset.
axes.consumer_uses_it_for: a must requirement in the fit column of the decision matrix

axes.means: The core reports which rows changed since the embedder last read them.
axes.consumer_uses_it_for: a important requirement in the fit column of the decision matrix

axes.means: The whole terminal state (screen, scrollback or cursor, modes) can be serialised or re-emitted so a second copy, attached later, can be brought to the same state.
axes.consumer_uses_it_for: a important requirement in the fit column of the decision matrix

axes.means: The embedder reads the program's output itself and hands the bytes to the core; the core does not insist on owning the read loop or the pseudoterminal.
axes.consumer_uses_it_for: a must requirement in the fit column of the decision matrix

axes.means: Answers the core generates for the program (device attributes, size reports, graphics query replies) are handed to the embedder, which decides where to write them.
axes.consumer_uses_it_for: a must requirement in the fit column of the decision matrix

axes.means: The core's state can be owned by one thread and handed to or shared with another behind a lock (it is Send), as when a parsing thread and a drawing thread both touch it.
axes.consumer_uses_it_for: a important requirement in the fit column of the decision matrix

axes.means: The embedder can read each picture a program placed: which image, the cell where it starts, how many cells it covers, and the image's pixels.
axes.consumer_uses_it_for: a must requirement in the fit column of the decision matrix

axes.means: The core resolves Kitty Unicode placeholder cells, telling the embedder which picture and which slice of it each placeholder cell shows.
axes.consumer_uses_it_for: a important requirement in the fit column of the decision matrix

axes.means: The embedder can refuse pictures sent as a file path, a temporary file or shared memory, while still accepting pictures sent inline.
axes.consumer_uses_it_for: a nice requirement in the fit column of the decision matrix

axes.means: how many must-have requirements the evidence shows the core does not meet
axes.compute: (1 if axis.cell_contents == 'does_not' else 0) + (1 if axis.zero_width == 'does_not' else 0) + (1 if axis.wide_chars == 'does_not' else 0) + (1 if axis.scrollback_read == 'does_not' else 0) + (1 if axis.feed_loop == 'does_not' else 0) + (1 if axis.replies_out == 'does_not' else 0) + (1 if axis.placements_readable == 'does_not' else 0)
axes.consumer_uses_it_for: a core with a must-have gap needs a line of TD code or a patch upstream before it can serve TD; shown as a count beside the fit

axes.means: how many of the eight interface fields the research filled
axes.consumer_uses_it_for: a thin dossier explains a column of evidence_silent; drawn beside the fit

axes.means: how settled the interface TD would depend on is
axes.consumer_uses_it_for: the stability column: an unstable or dormant interface is a cost TD pays on every upgrade, or never gets to pay

record.must_have_gaps: integer | null (null: a must-have answer is missing)

output.combination: version 1: the fit shown in the matrix is computed by scripts/matrix.py from these answers with weights 3/2/1 (must/important/nice), provides = 1, provides_with_work = 0.5, does_not = 0, evidence_silent excluded from both numerator and denominator and reported as coverage
output.unknown_rendering: evidence_silent and contested answers render as a grey cell labelled 'not established', never as a zero

evidence.<field>.recorded_by_research_ag.from: reported by the research agent's summary
evidence.<field>.recorded_by_research_ag.absent: omit: the field was not gathered

evidence.<field>.quoted_from_source.from: the passage the agent says it copied

evidence.<field>.claim_check_verdict.from: claim-check's verdict when it was not 'supported'

evidence.measured_by_bake_off.observed.from: the bake-off harnesses (bake/corebake, bake/ghostbake), for the four cores it ran
evidence.measured_by_bake_off.observed.absent: omit: the core was not run

core_evidence.snapshot: the research-delight run plus the claim-check run it was built from

maturity.<field>.recorded_by_research_ag.from: reported by the research agent: api_stability, latest_release, releases_last_12mo, maintainers

maturity.<field>.claim_check_verdict.from: claim-check's verdict when it was not 'supported'

instructions.question: Does `candidate` meet this requirement, judging only from `evidence`?
instructions.requirement: An embedder can read each visible cell's character, its foreground and background colour, and its attribute flags (bold, italic, underline, inverse).
instructions.judge_by: what `evidence` records and quotes about the core's interface; an entry carrying a "claim_check_verdict" was not confirmed by its own quote and counts for less

provides.means: `evidence` shows the core offering this directly: a type, method, callback or setting that does it.

provides_with_work.means: `evidence` shows the core has what is needed, but the embedder must assemble it: combine several calls, track state itself, or read an internal field.
provides_with_work.not_for: A capability the evidence shows missing.

does_not.means: `evidence` shows the core does not offer this, or offers it in a form that rules the requirement out.

evidence_silent.means: `evidence` does not say either way.
evidence_silent.not_for: A case where the evidence says the capability is absent: that is does_not.

instructions.question: Which describes the interface `candidate` would give Terminal Delight to depend on, judging only from `maturity`?
instructions.judge_by: what the project says about its API and what its release and commit history show, not how capable it is

stable_contract.means: The project promises a stable interface: version 1.0 or later with semantic versioning, or an explicit statement that the API is stable.

active_pre_1_0.means: Pre-1.0 and actively released, with breaking changes arriving in ordinary releases and no promise either way.
active_pre_1_0.not_for: A project that says outright that its API is unstable or experimental.

declared_unstable.means: The project itself says the interface is unstable, experimental, or expected to break.

dormant.means: No releases and no meaningful commits in the last year: the interface is frozen because nobody is working on it.

owned_by_td.means: The interface is Terminal Delight's own code, or a fork TD would carry itself.

not_established.means: `maturity` does not say enough to tell.

provides.means: the capability is there as an interface TD can call

provides_with_work.means: TD would write glue: the migration cost lives here

does_not.means: a gap TD must fill itself or a reason to rule the core out (a must-have)

evidence_silent.means: the research did not establish it: unknown, drawn grey, never scored as zero

confusable.means: an interface that exists but needs glue; either reading is a pass
the evidence mentions the area without settling it
the evidence shows the parts but not whether they reach the embedder (v1: rio-vt's placements at 0.46 against 0.52)

expect.why: the rubric asked for grid_api, state_snapshot, threading_and_loop and reply_channel on every subject; references like zellij-grid and td-own-core will be thinner

declared_unstable.means: The project itself says the interface is unstable, experimental, or expected to break.

dormant.means: No releases and no meaningful commits in the last year: the interface is frozen because nobody is working on it.

owned_by_td.means: The interface is Terminal Delight's own code, or a fork TD would carry itself.

not_established.means: `maturity` does not say enough to tell.

confidence_bands.means: two trajectories are live, usually active_pre_1_0 against declared_unstable

confusable.means: a pre-1.0 project that also warns about breakage; both count against stability

expect.why: almost every emulator core is pre-1.0; libvterm and vt100 look dormant; the keep-alacritty options partly own their code

invariants.means: Jev read a placement interface into a core the research says implements no Kitty feature
